name: CSCV Overfit Probability Gate with Median-Rank Parameter Choice
note: Runs Bailey/Borwein/Lopez de Prado/Zhu's combinatorially symmetric cross-validation over the family's OWN parameter grid (eight trend configurations, long above SMA(L), short below), enumerating every split of the trailing window into S/2 training blocks and their complement. PBO is the share of splits where the in-sample-best column lands below the out-of-sample median; the family trades only while PBO < pbo_max and the median OOS Sharpe of the chosen column is positive, and the configuration deployed is the highest MEDIAN-RANK column across all test sets, never the full-sample argmax. The source's two retirement rules are swept switches (`retire` = permanent retirement above pbo_retire, `slope_gate` = retirement on a negative IS-on-OOS degradation slope) because measured on real bars each of them retires everything -- with J and J' complementary halves of one window the slope is mechanically about -1 at every re-test. Deviations: S = 8 or 12 blocks rather than 16, and enumerations larger than `cap` are thinned by a fixed stride so the result stays deterministic. `slope_gate` stays a parameter rather than a swept one: on every re-test on all four probe symbols the slope came out near -1, so switching it on retires the family immediately and the sweep would spend half its budget on a known off switch.
source: Bailey, D., Borwein, J., Lopez de Prado, M. & Zhu, Q. (2017), 'The Probability of Backtest Overfitting', Journal of Computational Finance 20(4), 39-69 - Algorithm 2.3 (CSCV), Definition 2.2 (PBO), and Section 3 (performance degradation, probability of loss, stochastic dominance). Working paper PDF: https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/backtest-prob.pdf
code:
LOOK = [10, 20, 30, 50, 80, 120, 200, 300]


def family_init(ctx):
    """CSCV: score the OPTIMISER, then deploy the median-rank configuration.

    The family's own parameter grid is N trend configurations, column j being
    long while close > SMA(LOOK[j]) and short below it, so every column has the
    same gross exposure and their Sharpes are directly comparable. Their
    per-bar P&L forms the T x N matrix M.

    Every `retest` bars, on the trailing `win` bars:
      * split the rows into S contiguous, disjoint, equal blocks;
      * for every combination c of S/2 blocks, the training set J is those
        blocks and the test set J' is the complement;
      * n*(c) = argmax Sharpe on J; rbar = its rank among all N columns'
        Sharpes on J'; omega_c = rbar/(N+1); lambda_c = logit(omega_c);
      * PBO = the share of combinations with lambda_c < 0.
    Block sums of P&L and P&L^2 make the Sharpe of any union of blocks exact
    and O(S), which is what makes the full enumeration affordable.

    The family may trade only while PBO < pbo_max and the MEDIAN out-of-sample
    Sharpe of n*(c) is positive. Two retirement rules from the source are
    SWITCHES rather than hard-wired, because measured on this data both of them
    retire everything:
      retire=1     PBO above pbo_retire retires the family permanently, as
                   written; retire=0 lets a later re-test re-admit it.
      slope_gate=1 a negative degradation slope (OOS Sharpe regressed on IS
                   Sharpe across combinations) retires it regardless of PBO.
    The slope is measured either way. Note what it measures here: J and J' are
    complementary halves of ONE window, so a column that does well on J has
    mechanically done worse on J'; across eight highly correlated trend
    configurations that seesaw dominates and the slope came out near -1 at
    every single re-test on all four probe symbols. As a live gate it is an
    off switch, so it is swept rather than assumed.

    The deployed configuration is NOT the full-sample argmax: it is the column
    with the highest MEDIAN RANK across all test sets.

    Two more deviations, stated: S = 8 or 12 blocks rather than 16, because an
    intraday research window has nothing like the rows for 16 blocks of usable
    length; and if C(S, S/2) exceeds `cap` the enumeration is thinned by a
    fixed stride, which keeps it deterministic and re-runnable.
    """
    import math
    from itertools import combinations
    bars = ctx.bars
    m = len(bars)
    c = [float(b["c"]) for b in bars]
    N = len(LOOK)

    # ---- the N configurations and their per-bar P&L ----
    pos = [[0] * m for _ in range(N)]
    for j in range(N):
        L = LOOK[j]
        row = pos[j]
        s = 0.0
        for i in range(m):
            s += c[i]
            if i >= L:
                s -= c[i - L]
            if i >= L - 1:
                row[i] = 1 if c[i] > s / L else -1
    pnl = [[0.0] * m for _ in range(N)]
    for j in range(N):
        p = pos[j]
        q = pnl[j]
        for i in range(1, m):
            q[i] = p[i - 1] * (c[i] - c[i - 1])

    S = max(4, int(ctx.p.blocks))
    if S % 2:
        S += 1
    win = max(S * 40, int(ctx.p.win))
    retest = max(20, int(ctx.p.retest))
    cap = max(50, int(ctx.p.cap))
    pbo_max = float(ctx.p.pbo_max)
    pbo_ret = float(ctx.p.pbo_retire)

    combos = list(combinations(range(S), S // 2))
    if len(combos) > cap:
        stride = len(combos) // cap + 1
        combos = combos[::stride]
    ncb = len(combos)

    dep = [-1] * m           # deployed column, -1 = not trading
    live = -1
    dead = False
    for i in range(m):
        if not dead and i % retest == 0 and i >= win:
            lo = i - win + 1
            bl = win // S
            ns = [[0] * S for _ in range(N)]
            s1 = [[0.0] * S for _ in range(N)]
            s2 = [[0.0] * S for _ in range(N)]
            for b in range(S):
                a0 = lo + b * bl
                a1 = a0 + bl
                for j in range(N):
                    q = pnl[j]
                    t1 = 0.0
                    t2 = 0.0
                    for t in range(a0, a1):
                        x = q[t]
                        t1 += x
                        t2 += x * x
                    ns[j][b] = bl
                    s1[j][b] = t1
                    s2[j][b] = t2

            def sharpe(j, blocks):
                n = 0
                a = 0.0
                b2 = 0.0
                for b in blocks:
                    n += ns[j][b]
                    a += s1[j][b]
                    b2 += s2[j][b]
                if n < 20:
                    return None
                mu = a / n
                var = b2 / n - mu * mu
                if var <= 0.0:
                    return None
                return mu / math.sqrt(var)

            nlt = 0
            oos_star = []
            is_star = []
            rank_acc = [[] for _ in range(N)]
            used = 0
            for cb in combos:
                tr = cb
                te = tuple(b for b in range(S) if b not in cb)
                si = [sharpe(j, tr) for j in range(N)]
                so = [sharpe(j, te) for j in range(N)]
                if None in si or None in so:
                    continue
                used += 1
                star = max(range(N), key=lambda j: si[j])
                order = sorted(range(N), key=lambda j: so[j])
                for r, j in enumerate(order):
                    rank_acc[j].append(r + 1)
                rbar = order.index(star) + 1
                om = rbar / (N + 1.0)
                if om < 0.5:
                    nlt += 1
                oos_star.append(so[star])
                is_star.append(si[star])
            if used >= max(4, ncb // 4):
                pbo = nlt / float(used)
                srt = sorted(oos_star)
                med = srt[len(srt) // 2]
                mx = sum(is_star) / used
                my = sum(oos_star) / used
                cov = 0.0
                vx = 0.0
                for a in range(used):
                    dx = is_star[a] - mx
                    cov += dx * (oos_star[a] - my)
                    vx += dx * dx
                slope = cov / vx if vx > 0.0 else 0.0
                bad = pbo > pbo_ret or (ctx.p.slope_gate and slope < 0.0)
                if bad:
                    dead = bool(ctx.p.retire)
                    live = -1
                elif pbo < pbo_max and med > 0.0:
                    mr = []
                    for j in range(N):
                        v = sorted(rank_acc[j])
                        mr.append(v[len(v) // 2] if v else 0)
                    live = max(range(N), key=lambda j: mr[j])
                else:
                    live = -1
        dep[i] = live

    ctx.dep = ctx.series(dep, "deployed")
    ctx.pos = [ctx.series(pos[j], "cfg%d" % j) for j in range(N)]


def signal(ctx, i):
    j = ctx.dep[i]
    if j is None or j < 0:
        return 0
    p = ctx.pos[j][i]
    return 1 if p > 0 else (-1 if p < 0 else 0)
